newsitem.title: USA: Paxar to buy International Imaging for $200 million.
newsitem.headline: Paxar to buy International Imaging for $200 million.

text.p: Clothing label maker Paxar Corp. said Wednesday it is buying International Imaging Materials for $200 million in stock or $24 a share.

Following the news, the stock of International Imaging, which makes ribbons to print bar codes, jumped $7 to $23.50 on the Nasdaq market, while Paxar was up 87.5 cents at $19.19 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Under the deal, International Imaging stockholders will receive between 1.2 and 1.412 shares of Paxar common stock in exchange for each share of International Imaging, Paxar said.
The acquisition is expected to be treated as a tax-free exchange of shares.
The exchange ratio will be determined prior to the deal's closing, which is expected to take place in the fourth quarter. It will be based on Paxar's average price per share during a pricing period.

"This transaction will enhance our position in the rapidly growing automatic identification and tracking industry, Paxar Chairman Arthur Hershaft said in a statement. "We believe that this is particularly important in a time of industry consolidation."
